_comment: Canonical CortexSim identity-harness spec — the SINGLE source of truth shared by the push-mode bash generator (core/engine/push_generator.py via core/engine/identity_spec.py) and the pull-mode Go beacon (agent/identity, validated against this file by harness_spec_test.go). A scenario step's `identity` is a USERNAME string; both execution paths resolve it to the same {mode, wrapper} so a scenario behaves identically on push and pull. GAP-PUSH-001.

modes.direct: run the command as-is (no impersonation wrapper)

windows._comment: Windows has NO unattended impersonation primitive available to the beacon: runuser/sudo/su are POSIX-only and runas requires an interactive password prompt. Every non-direct identity therefore collapses to `direct` on Windows and MUST be reported as a degradation in the run record — a step that claims to have run as `administrator` while running as the beacon account is a correctness lie a POV readout would be built on. The single exception is when the beacon process is ALREADY running as the requested principal (e.g. installed as a service under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM), which is verified against the real process token, not assumed. Enforced by agent/identity/platform.go (ResolveFor) and guarded by harness_spec_test.go.
windows.resolution: direct (degraded) — unless the beacon's own account matches the requested identity, in which case it is honoured

_windows_identities_comment: Accounts the corpus declares on windows-ONLY steps. They are never impersonated — Windows has no unattended primitive, so ResolveFor collapses them to `direct` and records the degradation, exactly as it does for a service account. They are listed separately from service_accounts because a POSIX beacon must NOT treat them as known: `runuser -l administrator` on Linux is a scenario-authoring error, and S-17 rejects it rather than letting it fail on a customer's host.
